summary: Real tabbouleh, a Middle Eastern herb salad with just a little fine bulghur: 4 bunches of parsley and 2 of mint, washed, scrupulously dried and finely minced, tossed with soaked, wrung-out and chilled bulghur, tomato, cucumber, green onion, olive oil and lemon; serves 4.
glance: 1/2 cup fine, soaked 10 minutes in boiling water, squeezed dry in a towel, chilled at least 15 minutes
4 bunches flat-leaf parsley and 2 bunches mint, stems removed
Vegetarian and vegan (try cooked quinoa for gluten-free)
faq: What is real tabbouleh?

In the Middle East, an herb salad with a little bit of bulghur wheat for texture. In the US it usually becomes a soggy bulghur salad with a sad speck of parsley. The star ingredients are parsley and mint seasoned with plenty of olive oil and lemon juice.
How do I mince the herbs?

Wash the leaves, dry them completely (a salad spinner works well), gather them in a tight bunch and slice as thinly as possible, then go back and forth over them on the board with a rocking motion. The author notes his in the photo weren't minced quite fine enough.
Why wring out the bulghur?
Don't skip squeezing the soaked bulghur dry in a dish towel and chilling it briefly: if it's wet or hot it will ruin the tabbouleh.
How should tabbouleh be dressed?
Quite well dressed and piquant, but not sitting in a puddle of dressing. Taste and add more salt, olive oil or lemon juice.
What do I serve with it?
A Middle Eastern feast of hummus, baba ghanouj, falafel and lots of pita, or stuff it in a pita sandwich.

summary: Basic pastry dough for tender, flaky crusts: 1 cup flour, a pinch of salt and 6 tablespoons very cold butter cut in to an oatmeal texture in under 2 minutes, bound with 2-4 tablespoons ice water, chilled at least an hour (up to two days) and rolled out; 30 minutes active.
glance: 1 cup flour, 6 tablespoons very cold butter, 2-4 tablespoons ice water
at least 1 hour and up to 2 days
a pastry blender, two knives, fingers or a food processor
faq: What is the goal of pastry dough?
To get well-distributed pockets of butter that separate layers of the dough while minimizing gluten development.
Do I need a pastry blender?
The author likes one because his hands are too warm and a food processor dirties more. Without one, use two butter knives, your fingers, or pulse in a food processor, stopping at the oatmeal stage.
How much water do I add?

Start with 2 tablespoons of ice water, work it in with a fork for 60 seconds, and see if a piece presses into a ball. If not, add more ice water a couple of teaspoons at a time. Err on the side of minimal water; a little unincorporated flour is fine. The amount depends on the moisture in your flour and butter.
How long should I work the butter in?
At most 2 minutes, until it mostly looks like coarse oatmeal. Some larger chunks of butter are fine.
How do I roll it out?
Chill the dough at least an hour, let it warm until slightly pliable (5 to 20 minutes), give it several thwacks while still wrapped, then roll it on a floured board to the shape you need.

summary: An anti-griddle pudding pop with bruleed mango and a black sesame tuile, the author's MasterChef audition dish: chocolate pudding frozen on a homemade dry-ice anti-griddle, a torched mango, and a kaffir lime and ginger coconut milk sauce thickened with Ultra-Tex 3; written as a single serving.
glance: homebrew: dry ice between two sheet pans or cake pans
1 can coconut milk infused 30 minutes with kaffir lime leaves and ginger, thickened with Ultra-Tex 3
faq: What is an anti-griddle?

Popular in modern-style restaurants: a flat griddle surface under which liquid nitrogen circulates so you can freeze a liquid in seconds. The author made a home version with dry ice between two sheet pans or cake pans.
Is dry ice safe to use?
The author says if you try it, use gloves and be careful: touching dry ice can hurt you badly.
How do I freeze things on it?

Use a slightly thickened liquid so you can control how it spreads, and lightly wipe the surface with oil to make it easier to release your food. The author has frozen yogurts, puddings and sauces this way.
What is Ultra-Tex 3?

A modified food starch that thickens at room temperature, which makes it easy to see when you've reached the desired texture, so you don't need to be as precise as with some other hydrocolloids. It releases flavor well and doesn't get gummy.
Where did the recipe come from?

It was the author's dish for the Seattle MasterChef auditions, with no cooking facilities, so he made a dessert allowing last-minute cooking with his own tools; it earned a callback. Pudding follows a Smitten Kitchen formula with good dark chocolate, and tuiles from Cooking Debauchery with black sesame paste.

summary: Pan-roasted Brussels sprouts with shiitakes and smoked paprika: sliced shiitake caps browned about a minute per side, then quartered sprouts cooked in the same pan until nearly charred, tossed with smoked paprika and salt and finished with pepper and Maldon; 7 ingredients, 10-15 minutes, serves 2-3.
glance: 3 cups quartered (about 9 ounces), cooked over medium-high heat until many dark brown spots
faq: Why are Brussels sprouts popular now?

They had underdog status because they were boiled to death for much of the 20th century, but they are delicious when pan-fried, deep-fried, broiled, roasted or otherwise subjected to high heat for shorter periods. The author still likes them steamed or boiled with sweet butter if not overcooked.
How do I cook them so they're nearly charred?
In the skillet over medium-high heat with a shimmering layer of oil, turn occasionally until tender and many surfaces have dark brown spots; the author likes them almost charred.
What does smoked paprika do?

It takes any dish and makes it taste like it was cooked over an open wood fire. Together with Maldon salt, which adds a flaky saline crunch as a finishing touch, the author calls them two ingredients that will change your life as a cook.
How do I cook the shiitakes?
Cook the 1/8-inch slices in a single layer until well browned on one side, about one minute, then flip; remove to paper towels, leaving the oil behind, and salt. Add them back at the end.
What other vegetable is cooked hard and fast?
The author suggests lemony grilled gai lan (Chinese broccoli).

summary: Mexican panzanella salad: a lime, olive oil, garlic, ancho and cumin dressing tossed with roasted poblanos, heirloom tomatoes, cucumber, corn, red onion, diced ciabatta, avocado and a mix of cilantro, parsley and mint, rested a few minutes; serves 8 as most of dinner.
glance: 8 as most of dinner (easily halved for a side)
5 small limes, 3/4 cup olive oil, garlic, ancho chili powder, cumin; should be pretty salty
1 loaf ciabatta, stale or toasted, medium dice (corn tortillas for gluten-free)
faq: What is panzanella?

An Italian bread salad. This Mexican version swaps in poblanos, corn, avocado, lime, ancho and cumin. The idea is loosely based on the title of a Rick Bayless recipe, though the author's version has nothing in common with Bayless's chayote-based one.
When do I add the bread?

If you like the bread to sop up the juice, add it with the vegetables; otherwise wait until close to serving time. Combine everything about 15 minutes before serving, toss gently but thoroughly, and let it rest a few minutes.
How do I make it gluten-free?
Use corn tortillas instead of the bread.
How salty should the dressing be?
Pretty salty, since it dresses a big pile of vegetables and bread.
Can I change it?

Add jalapeno or other hot peppers to amp it up, change the vegetables to what's fresh and in season, and perhaps add lime zest to the dressing. The recipe fed 6 with one other dish and lots of leftovers, so it can be halved for a side.

summary: Grilled flatbread with Padron peppers and zucchini blossoms: a yeasted dough with a little rye flour (ideally rested overnight in the refrigerator), rolled into 12 x 4-inch loaves, grilled on hot coals and topped with blistered Padron peppers, halved blossoms and fresh chevre.
glance: rest overnight in the refrigerator (retarding), or let rise a couple of hours the same day
24 Padron peppers, 12 zucchini blossoms halved lengthwise, 12 ounces chevre
grill on hot coals, oiled side down until golden, then flip
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the chevre
faq: What are Padron peppers?

A Spanish variety frequently served for tapas, traditionally pan-fried in olive oil and served whole with plenty of flaky sea salt. They have a more complex flavor than green bell peppers but are a gamble on the Scoville scale: some are completely tame and others as hot as a serrano.
How do I buy zucchini blossoms?
If you can buy them still attached to baby squash they are often a better deal: they stay fresh longer and you get tiny squash in the bargain. Cut them in half lengthwise to show off their interior.
What is the difference between flatbread and pizza?

There isn't a definitive difference, but the author calls it flatbread if there's no sauce or thick layer of cheese. You can also bake it in the oven, preferably on a pizza stone, or on a baking sheet at 450°F.
What does retarding the dough mean?

Making the dough a day in advance and resting it in the refrigerator overnight: slowing the rise allows more complex flavors to develop. Take it out about 2 hours before rolling. Same-day dough needs a couple of hours to rise.
Why add rye flour?
For added flavor, as recommended in Alice Waters' The Art of Simple Food; use more white flour if you don't have rye.

summary: Easy eggplant and ricotta rolls with ajvar: peeled eggplant slabs roasted at 375°F until thoroughly tender, filled with 2 tablespoons of seasoned fresh ricotta each, folded, and drizzled with ajvar (Balkan roasted red pepper spread) or tomato sauce and parsley; serves 4, at room temperature.
glance: 1 large, peeled, 8 slabs about 1/3 to 1/2 inch thick
375°F until thoroughly tender, checking after 15 minutes
1 jar ajvar or 1 cup thick tomato sauce
faq: What is ajvar?

A mild spread of roasted red peppers popular throughout the Balkans, fairly easy to find at gourmet grocery stores, with spicy versions too. The author has loved it for years because it's inexpensive and full of flavor, eaten on eggs, on toast with melted cheese, and by the tablespoonful.
What can I use instead of ajvar?
A simple, slightly thick, flavorful tomato sauce (the author likes a five-minute tomato sauce from Heidi). Feta would be another filling choice if you want to continue with Balkan flavors.
How do I choose eggplant?
Look for ones that feel heavy for their size, which means the flesh will be firm, not spongy; the author's felt twice as heavy as expected.
How do I know the eggplant is done?
Roast until thoroughly tender, checking every few minutes after 15 minutes. There is nothing nastier than undercooked eggplant, so if in doubt go a little farther.
How do I assemble the rolls?

Carefully transfer each slab to a platter so it doesn't rip, fill with about 2 tablespoons of seasoned ricotta, fold in half, arrange in a line, and pour sauce down the middle. Finish with salt, pepper, parsley and olive oil, and serve at room temperature.

summary: Quinoa with tahina sauce, tofu and green beans, the author's "glorious hippie food": rinsed quinoa simmered 15-18 minutes in a 2:1 ratio, steamed green beans, browned tofu cubes and a lemon-garlic tahini sauce thinned with warm water; serves 4 as a main.
glance: 1.5 cups, rinsed twice, simmered 15-18 minutes with 3 cups water
1 cup tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt, thinned with warm water
faq: Why must quinoa be rinsed?
It needs to be rinsed a couple of times in cold water because the grain has a slightly bitter coating (saponins). Some boxed quinoa may already have it removed, but the author wouldn't count on it.
How do I cook quinoa?

Simmer in a pot with a 2:1 ratio of water, covered on low, for 15-18 minutes until the water is absorbed, or cook it in a rice cooker with the same ratio. Fluff it and let it rest about 5 minutes with the cover off to get rid of excess steam.
How do I make tahina sauce?

A classic combination of plain tahini with garlic and lemon juice: whiz tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt until smooth, adding warm water, possibly quite a lot, to reach sauce consistency. Don't serve "mortar paste." Leave it in the machine until serving time because it thickens, and give it one last spin.
Which tahini should I buy?
Joyva or Alwadi are good brands, or any Middle Eastern brand; if you use a health-food type brand, look for one that specifies toasted, not raw, which the author finds yucky.
Why quinoa with sesame?
The author finds quinoa has an affinity for sesame, maybe because both are mild and nutty. Quinoa, tofu and sesame are also all high-protein, nutritionally dense foods.

summary: Pumpkin ravioli with a simple vegetable broth and white beans, after Paul Bertolli's Cooking by Hand: a rustic filling of roasted sugar pumpkin, onion, garlic, sage, cream, cheese and nutmeg bound with egg, served in a broth of caramelized leeks, carrot, celery and beans simmered at least 30 minutes; serves at least 4.
glance: 1 sugar pumpkin (about 3 pounds) roasted at 400°F, smashed with sauteed aromatics, cream and cheese
caramelized leeks, carrots, celery, beans, bay leaves and optionally a parmesan rind, simmered at least 1/2 hour
Vegetarian; filling is gluten-free but the ravioli wouldn't be
faq: How was the dish served?

Three ways from one batch: with brown butter and crispy sage, over a rustic broth with caramelized leeks, carrots, celery and white beans, and with brown butter plus big doses of smoked paprika and black pepper. The author froze half the ravioli.
How do I make the pumpkin filling?

Roast the pumpkin at 400°F until easily pierced, saute onion, garlic, chili flakes, sage and salt in butter until the onion begins to brown, scoop the pumpkin into the pan and smash with cream, cheese and nutmeg until a fairly uniform thick filling, cool a bit and stir in the eggs. It's meant to be rustic; use a food mill for smooth.
Any tips for ravioli dough?
For filled pasta, make the dough slightly wetter than normal so it is easier to seal reliably. The author doesn't give the pasta recipe because it would need a whole photo tutorial.
What do I do with extra filling?
Spread it in a shallow baking dish, top with a bit of cheese and bake at 350°F for a nice gratin.
Why add a parmesan rind to the broth?

The author scrubs and freezes parmesan rinds because they add a delicious layer of flavor to this kind of soup; you can make it without. The more browning the vegetables get, the more flavor the soup develops.

summary: Figs with ricotta, honey and several little garnishes: ripe figs cut into odd-shaped pieces with Calabro ricotta quenelles, blackberry honey, lime zest, tarragon, crushed saffron and a few crystals of pyramidal salt; serves 4 in 5 minutes, a concept for barely manipulated ingredients.
glance: 1/2 cup Calabro ricotta, formed in quenelles
blackberry honey, lime zest, tarragon, saffron, pyramidal sea salt, in tiny amounts
faq: What is the concept?

Using simple but fantastic ingredients and doing almost nothing to them. The many small adornments work because most are used in tiny amounts, so each bite is different: citrus, then herb, then the metallic tang of saffron.
How do I cut the figs?
Add visual interest by cutting each fig "randomly" into 3 odd-shaped pieces, not parallel or perpendicular to the base.
Can I change the ingredients?

Absolutely: the same idea works with a perfect peach. Lime could be lemon or yuzu or nothing; tarragon could be shiso, basil or anise hyssop; honey could be elderberry syrup or a drizzle of good balsamic.
What ricotta should I use?
Calabro ricotta, which the author calls the only national ricotta worthy of the name, or homemade.
Where can I find flavor combinations?
The author mentions Cuuks.com as a great free tool for discovering and storing flavor combinations.
